subject: Re: Private DNS authorization, proxying, and TLS handoff — end-to-end checklist
messages:
From: James Shephard <j.shephard@acme.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudProxy Ops <ops@cloudproxy.example.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Private DNS proof + question on TLS termination

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. We captured the ACL and zone delegation steps on our side — attached is the signed DNS proof bundle that shows the NS delegation and the TXT ownership token we put in acme-internal.example.

Before we finalize the MPA, two quick clarifying questions for your engineering team: 
1) For inbound requests from our clients to the private endpoint, do you expect Redwood to terminate TLS at the VPC edge (Redwood-managed proxy) or should we provision a customer cert and keep termination on our side?
2) If Redwood terminates, what exact SANs and subject formats do you need in the customer cert to ensure the SNI mapping is stable across failover?

We want to avoid last-minute cert mismatches during the cutover window.

Attached: acme-dns-proof.pdf

Best,
James
SRE, Acme Corp
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: James Shephard <j.shephard@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, CloudProxy Ops <ops@cloudproxy.example.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 17:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private DNS proof + question on TLS termination

Hi James — thanks for the bundle, it looks good on quick inspection. A few things from the Redwood side to clarify so we can align the checklist and the MPA signature: 

- Termination options: we support both models but recommend Redwood edge termination for predictable latency and simplified rotation unless you require client certs inside your environment for policy reasons.
  - Redwood-managed termination: Redwood deploys a per-tenant proxy in your VPC (dedicated/pooled depending on commitment). We present the upstream certificate (we can either use a Redwood-managed cert or attach your supplied certificate to the proxy).
  - Customer-side termination: You terminate in your environment and Redwood routes via the configured proxy using mutual TLS for the control plane and TLS for data path.

- SAN requirements if Redwood terminates: wildcard not allowed for internal-only namespaces. Preferred subject patterns: CN=acme-internal.example, SANs: acme-internal.example, *.acme-internal.example (only if you accept internal wildcard policies). We also need a stable metadata label (tenant-id) encoded in the certificate's OU to tie the cert to the routing rule.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik and Kimberly — can you confirm the exact OU label string and the expected cert validity window Redwood will accept for initial onboarding?
2) James — if you prefer Redwood-managed certs, confirm scope (we will generate CSR and provide CSR proof request). If you prefer to upload your cert, share the preferred rotation cadence and the KMS/HSM key reference.

Copying ops at CloudProxy for networking handoff.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: acme-dns-proof.pdf]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, James Shephard <j.shephard@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, CloudProxy Ops <ops@cloudproxy.example.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private DNS proof + question on TLS termination

Thanks Naomi. For the OU label we typically request: OU=tenant:acme-corp (ascii, no spaces). We'll accept cert validity up to 24 months for initial onboarding but request rotation reminders at 60/30/7 days. If Acme wants Redwood-managed certs, our CSR flow produces a CSR ID and we expect the final cert in PEM with chain and intermediate(s) attached.

A few operational constraints to call out so Acme can validate with their security team: 
- If Redwood manages termination, we will allocate a proxy IP inside your VPC; the egress route from that proxy to Redwood control plane will use mutual TLS and must appear in your firewall allowlist (CloudProxy will coordinate).
- SNI routing uses the exact hostname in the SAN; any SAN mismatch across rollover will cause a 421-style TLS handshake fail and will fall back to the secondary routing policy. To reduce risk, we recommend provisioning the current and next certs in parallel (blue/green attach) and keeping identical SAN order.

Attached: tls-handshake-diagram.png (shows expected SNI/TLS flow and fallback path).

Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: James Shephard <j.shephard@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private DNS proof + question on TLS termination

Appreciate the detail. Acme's security team prefers customer-side termination for initial rollouts but will accept Redwood-managed termination for dev/staging lanes to speed testing. Action items from our side:
- We'll provision a cert with OU=tenant:acme-corp and SANs = acme-internal.example + api.acme-internal.example and send the PEM chain by EOD tomorrow.
- We'll also whitelist outbound to the Redwood control plane IP ranges (provided in the MPA appendix).

Procurement: please find the updated MPA draft with the service appendix (we've redlined a request for a shorter rotation SLA on cert revocation).

James
SRE, Acme Corp
[Attachment referenced: mpa-sig-request.pdf]

Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private DNS proof + question on TLS termination

Thanks all — this is a good alignment. Summary and onboarding checklist (for our runbook):
- Acme will seed: DNS delegation (confirmed), cert PEM chain (OU=tenant:acme-corp), and firewall allowlist entries.
- Redwood will: provision VPC-side proxy, support both customer and Redwood termination lanes, provide CSR flow if requested, and schedule blue/green cert attach for rotation.
- CloudProxy: coordinate VPC route and NAT egress so control-plane MTLS endpoints are reachable; confirm IP ranges by Friday.
- Procurement/Legal: target signature on updated MPA by next Wednesday (2026-09-30).

Outstanding risks: cert chain ordering mistakes during handoff; ephemeral DNS TTL mismatches when flipping SNI rules. We'll run a pre-cutover validation: 1) CSR proof sign, 2) cert attach in staging with SNI verification, 3) controlled roll to production off-peak. Please confirm acceptance of the checklist items and any add-ons you want in the runbook.

Cheers,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Inline checklist included]
